scope: Calendar source removal revisions and recoverable source-wide purge with REST, CLI and browser controls; not full M4 acceptance
verifiedBehavior: Ordinary calendar source removal publishes new root/member revisions as one group and repeat removal does not revise documents again.
An authorized purge intent persists before file removal and continues after request interruption or revocation of the requesting credential.
Source purge erases the protected link, root and member payload lineage, projections and owned snapshots, including a never-imported source with only a candidate snapshot.
File removal uses bounded journal batches and successfully removes 1100 retained snapshots plus the accepted snapshot and a hidden trash original while preserving an unrelated file.
Recovery handles source-removal publication interruption, file quarantine, batch finalization, root finalization and never-accepted snapshot writes.
Strict purge scans ignore ingestion ignore files and reserved-directory skips, reject an owned symlink without following it, and keep the source purge pending until repaired.
Pending purge failures retain a sanitized error code and attempt time; recovery rotates attempts and continues other selected sources.
REST/CLI require an explicit purge selection and recent-password session; browser cancellation preserves events and confirmed purge removes their search results.
notes: A regression test found that normal folder scans omit symlinks, which could leave an owned file path behind during purge. Added a strict purge scanning mode while preserving the ingestion default.
A focused follow-up found InvalidDataException was not included in purge failure recording. The failure is now recorded and recoverable; the final full regression passed.
The first browser run passed before these scanner fixes. Final browser qualification was repeated on the final build, with all screenshots reviewed.
One expected browser console 404 came from deliberately checking that the purged source no longer exists. The page was closed before stopping the final fixture.
limitations: Folder-source purge is not implemented; purge requests for folder sources explicitly reject instead of silently performing ordinary removal.
The older direct container-document purge still has its original per-mutation file-count/metadata bounds; the calendar source purge workflow uses batches to handle larger snapshot histories.
General retention, removed identity expiry, encrypted backup/restore/export, remaining enrichment/provider/budget work and release supply-chain controls remain pending.
M4 production migration and final hardened deployment/live-feed/backup acceptance remain unqualified.
No production service, configuration, source or user data was changed.
